Special Thematic Breakdown of Key Quran Paras

Juz 2: Sayaqool (سَيَقُولُ)

Quran Para 2 (2nd Para of Quran / Second Para of Quran)

Opening with the momentous decree changing the Qibla (prayer orientation) from Jerusalem to the Holy Ka’bah in Makkah, quran para 2 lays the legislative foundations of the Muslim Ummah. It institutes the obligatory fasting of Ramadan (Al-Baqarah 2:183-187), rulings of marital relations, Hajj rites between Safa and Marwa, spending in charity, and concludes with the historic victory of Talut over Jalut (Goliath).

Juz 3: Tilkal Rusul (تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ)

3rd Para of Quran (Third Para of Quran)

The 3rd para of quran features the greatest verse in the entire revelation: Ayat al-Kursi (The Throne Verse, Al-Baqarah 2:255), declaring Allah’s absolute sovereignty and eternal life. It strictly forbids Riba (usury/interest), records the longest verse regarding debt contracts (Ayat ad-Dayn, 2:282), and transitions into Surah Ali ‘Imran with the miraculous birth of Maryam (Mary).

Juz 8: Wa Lau Annana (وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا)

Quran Para 8: Creation, Prophetic Missions & Dietary Laws

In quran para 8, the Quran presents extensive rational proofs of Divine unity in cosmic creation. It details lawful (Halal) and unlawful meat, delineates the ten moral commandments of Islam, and recounts the primordial dialogue between Allah and Iblis (Satan) at the creation of Adam. It proceeds into the harrowing histories of the peoples of Prophet Hud, Salih, Lut, and Shu’ayb.

Juz 29 & 30: Tabarakallazi & Amma

Quran Para 29 & Quran Para 30 (Juz Amma)

Quran para 29 opens with Surah Al-Mulk, protecting reciters from the torment of the grave. Quran para 30 (Juz Amma) contains 37 short, rhythmically powerful Makki surahs memorized by Muslims worldwide and recited in the daily Fard and Sunnah rakats of Salah, ending with the twin protective surahs Al-Falaq and An-Nas.

Sajdah at-Tilawah Manual

The 14 Sajdah Tilawat in the Holy Quran

According to the consensus of scholars across the Hanafi, Shafi’i, and Hanbali schools, there are exactly 14 agreed-upon Sajdah Tilawat (how many sajdah in quran). The first sajdah in quran occurs in Surah Al-A’raf (7:206) in Para 9.

#Surah NameVerse (Ayah)Para (Juz)Spiritual Context & Sign
1Al-A'raf7:206Para 9First Sajdah in Quran. Humility before the Creator alongside heavenly angels.
2Ar-Ra'd13:15Para 13All creation prostrates willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows.
3An-Nahl16:50Para 14Angels fear their Lord above them and carry out everything commanded.
4Al-Isra17:109Para 15The righteous fall down weeping upon hearing revelation, increasing in reverence.
5Maryam19:58Para 16When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited, prophets fell in prostration.
6Al-Hajj22:18Para 17The sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and living creatures all bow to Allah.
7Al-Furqan25:60Para 19Refusal of the disbelievers to prostrate to Ar-Rahman contrasted with the faithful.
8An-Naml27:26Para 19Allah: none has the right to be worshipped but He, Lord of the Supreme Throne.
9As-Sajdah32:15Para 21Only those believe who, when reminded, fall in prostration free from arrogance.
10Sad38:24Para 23Prophet Dawud fell down bowing and turning to Allah in repentance.
11Fussilat41:38Para 24Those in presence of your Lord glorify Him night and day and never tire.
12An-Najm53:62Para 27So prostrate to Allah and worship Him alone.
13Al-Inshiqaq84:21Para 30Rebuking those who do not prostrate when the Holy Quran is recited to them.
14Al-Alaq96:19Para 30Nay! Do not obey him, but prostrate yourself and draw near to Allah.

Method for Performing Sajdah Tilawat:

When reciting or listening to any of the 14 verses above, it is Wajib (in the Hanafi school) or Sunnah Mu’akkadah (in the Shafi’i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools) to perform prostration. While in a state of Wudu facing the Qibla, stand up and say “Allahu Akbar” (without raising your hands to the ears), prostrate directly onto the ground, recite “Subhana Rabbiyal A’la” three times, and then say “Allahu Akbar” to rise back up. No Tashahhud or Salam is required.

Completion Supplication

Dua Khatam Quran: Sacred Prayer upon Completing Recitation

Upon finishing the recitation of the 30th Para of the Holy Quran, the believer offers dua khatam quran. Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) used to gather his family upon completing the Quran to make heartfelt supplications together.

اللَّهُمَّ ارْحَمْنِي بِالْقُرْآنِ، وَاجْعَلْهُ لِي إِمَامًا وَنُورًا وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً، اللَّهُمَّ ذَكِّرْنِي مِنْهُ مَا نَسِيتُ، وَعَلِّمْنِي مِنْهُ مَا جَهِلْتُ، وَارْزُقْنِي تِلَاوَتَهُ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ، وَاجْعَلْهُ لِي حُجَّةً يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ

English Transliteration

“Allahumma irhamni bil-Qur’an, waj’alhu li imaman wa nuran wa hudan wa rahmah. Allahumma dhakkirni minhu ma nassitu, wa ‘allimni minhu ma jahiltu, warzuqni tilawatahu ana’a al-layli wa atraf an-nahar, waj’alhu li hujjatan ya Rabbal ‘Alameen.”

English Translation

“O Allah, have mercy upon me by the Quran, and make it for me a guide, a light, guidance, and mercy. O Allah, remind me of what I have forgotten from it, teach me what I am ignorant of from it, grant me its recitation during the hours of the night and at the ends of the day, and make it an argument in my favor, O Lord of the worlds.”

Frequently Asked Questions on the Holy Quran

The Holy Quran contains 30 Paras (Juz) and 114 Surahs. In the standard King Fahd Complex Madani Mushaf (15-line Uthmani script), there are exactly 604 pages, structured so that each Juz comprises 20 pages (with the 30th Juz covering 23 pages). Indo-Pak 16-line editions generally span 548 pages, and 13-line prints span 848 pages.
